correctness.rationale: For K algebraically closed characteristic zero, p nonconstant and q nonzero, rank inequality for all square X,Y implies by X=I,Y=J_a(lambda) that each root lambda of p occurs in q to at least the same multiplicity, hence p|q. If p(0)=0 and q has exactly the same zero multiplicity, X=J_{a+1}(0), Y=diag(1,...,1,0) makes p(XY)=0 and q(YX)!=0; thus tp|q. If p(0)!=0, intertwinings Yp(XY)=p(YX)Y and reverse, with Y injective on ker p(XY), force equal ranks of p(XY),p(YX); divisibility then gives domination with sharp C=1. When tp|q, free identity q(yx)=y p(xy) x r(yx) proves membership. Otherwise pick nonzero root lambda of p and unilateral L,R shifts LR=I, RL=I-P: p(lambda LR)=0 while q(lambda RL)e1=q(0)e1 !=0, separating ideal membership. Independently checked F3 every 2x2 X,Y pair (6561) for both sufficiency branches and nilpotent 2x2 failure witness. Infinite-dimensional representation is used as an algebra homomorphism and is not a finite matrix counterexample.

value.rationale: The first nonhomogeneous rank-Nullstellensatz counterexample is classified within a mathematically canonical product-reversal ansatz. The sharp dividing lines at p(0)=0 and the extra zero root show exactly when inequality is a genuine nonmembership witness, and prove collapse of every admissible C to 1; useful structural boundary, not an arbitrary reparameterization.
